intent.summary: Allow the review-packet/approval system to recognize when a branch has been history-rewritten (rebased) since the last reviewed packet, and to let an approver explicitly authorize a lease-scoped force-push to republish that exact rebased commit instead of silently treating it as an unreviewable gap.
intent.reasoning: The change introduces a `chain-break` concept across the packet model, renderer, bash glue scripts, and Clojure approval service, all gated on chain reasons `not-descendant`/`predecessor-head-missing`. It adds a brand-new `force-push` delivery option whose validity is tightly bound to a `lease` (the exact remote head recorded on the chain-break packet), mirroring git's `--force-with-lease` semantics — this is clearly solving 'the last reviewed commit no longer exists in history, so how do we safely let a reviewer re-publish the rewritten branch' (PER-128).

direct_impacts.description: New --remote-ref/--remote-head inputs and a chain-break record are threaded through packet construction and rendered as a dedicated warning section with SHA table and force-push explanation.
Adds a fourth delivery choice (force-push) gated by a server-computed lease, changes the 400/409 error contract, and changes what 'never' means depending on whether a lease is offered.

New 13th positional arg (lease), new validated `force-push` case that re-queries kk-approval status to confirm chain_break + matching remote_head before allowing the action, and new fields threaded through the event-fold state machine.
Reads local refs/remotes/origin/<branch> to capture remote-ref/remote-head without an explicit fetch step in the shown diff, feeding directly into the lease logic.

indirect_impacts.description: The `--action force-push --lease <sha>` contract is produced here but its consumer (the actual `git push --force-with-lease` invocation) is not part of this diff, so correctness of the safety guarantee cannot be verified from this change alone.

New keys (chain_break, remote_ref, remote_head, :chain-break) added to packet.json, approval facts JSON, and the canonical/public key allowlists in model.clj; any strict external JSON schema validators or downstream tooling not shown could reject or ignore these fields.

indirect_impacts.area: Narrative generation for non-incremental chain reasons
indirect_impacts.description: Reclassifying not-descendant/predecessor-head-missing as 'chain-break' changes the jq branch order in send_brief, altering what text reviewers/LLM narrators see for cases previously treated as generic 'full packet' reasons.

risks.description: A brand-new destructive capability (force-push) is being wired into an automated approval/dispatch pipeline; any gap in the gating logic could let a force-push proceed against the wrong commit or a non-chain-break packet.
risks.mitigation: Multiple layers are implemented: Clojure decide only accepts force-push if the session-stored `:lease` was set when choices were issued; kk-packet-approval.sh re-queries kk-approval status at decide time to confirm chain_break + matching remote_head + lease != head; downstream push is presumably `--force-with-lease`, which fails safely if remote has moved.
edge_cases: TOCTOU window between the status re-check in kk-packet-approval.sh and the actual push executed later by Gatekeeper

A stale local refs/remotes/origin tracking ref in kk-review-packet.sh causing a lease value that doesn't reflect true remote state (mitigated by force-with-lease failing safely, but not verified since Gatekeeper code isn't in this diff)
Multiple packets for the same ticket where an older packet's recorded chain_break/remote_head could satisfy the check if kk-approval status does not strictly return only the newest packet's facts

risks.description: The actual consumer of the new `--lease` flag (presumably Gatekeeper's push logic) is not part of this diff, so it's unverified whether the lease is actually passed to `git push --force-with-lease` or merely logged/ignored.
risks.mitigation: Verify Gatekeeper/dispatch code (not shown) honors the lease as the exact `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-sha>` value.
edge_cases: Lease silently dropped, resulting in an unconditional force-push
Lease applied to the wrong ref if `remote_ref` parsing/quoting is mishandled downstream

risks.description: No test files appear in the diff despite the project declaring 'Has Tests: Yes', for a change that expands destructive action surface and alters narrative/UI branching logic.
risks.mitigation: Confirm whether tests exist elsewhere/were run but not included in this commit's diff, or add targeted tests for chain-break detection, the force-push gate, and the Clojure decide error paths.
edge_cases: Regression in non-chain-break paths (e.g., existing `not-descendant` full-packet narrative) due to the new elif branch ordering in kk-packet.sh's jq filter

risks.description: UI/consequence text asserts strong guarantees ('refuses if the remote is anywhere else') that depend entirely on correct downstream enforcement not visible in this diff, risking false reassurance to human approvers.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the stated guarantee is actually enforced end-to-end before shipping the UI copy.
edge_cases: Approver trusts the message and approves, but a bug in dispatch performs a plain force-push without the lease check

review_questions.question: Where is the new `--lease` value actually consumed to perform `git push --force-with-lease`? Can you show the Gatekeeper/dispatch code path, since it's not part of this diff?
review_questions.context: The entire safety story for allowing force-push through an automated approval pipeline hinges on this being correctly wired; without seeing it, the gating logic added here could be necessary but not sufficient.

review_questions.question: Does `kk-approval status <ticket>` always report facts for the ticket's current/newest packet only, guaranteeing the force-push check in kk-packet-approval.sh can't be satisfied using a stale, superseded packet's chain_break/remote_head?
review_questions.context: The inline comment claims this invariant ('only while it is still this ticket's newest packet') but the jq filter itself doesn't visibly enforce it — it just matches on packet id.

review_questions.question: Is there a fetch step guaranteed immediately before kk-review-packet.sh reads refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, or could remote_head be built from an arbitrarily stale local tracking ref?
review_questions.context: Even though --force-with-lease fails safely on mismatch, a stale remote_head could cause confusing 'chain break' UI messaging or an unnecessary refusal/approval mismatch for reviewers relying on this page as ground truth.

review_questions.question: Are there automated tests covering the new chain-break classification, the force-push lease validation (both the Clojure decide 409 path and the shell re-check), and the render.clj break-section output?
review_questions.context: The project has test infrastructure, but no test changes accompany a change that adds a new destructive action path and multiple new branches in brief/narrative generation.

review_questions.question: Could `not-descendant` or `predecessor-head-missing` ever legitimately occur without an actual untrusted history rewrite (e.g., shallow clone artifacts, submodule quirks, or a squash-merge that's still content-equivalent), causing an unnecessary chain-break escalation and blocking the simpler incremental flow?
review_questions.context: Unconditionally treating these two reasons as `rewrites` changes both the narrative instructions and available approval choices; false positives would add friction, false negatives would under-protect.
